name: Question 9
worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the flight duration (in minutes). Then we have $X∼N(180,{20}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(178<X<188).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(178<X<188) & =P(\frac{178-180}{20}<Z<\frac{188-180}{20}) \\  & =P(-0.1<Z<0.4)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.1<Z<0.4) & =P(Z<0.4)-P(Z\le -0.1) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.4)-P(Z\le -0.1) \\  & =Φ(0.4)-Φ(-0.1)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.4) & =0.6554 \\ Φ(-0.1) & =0.4602.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.1<Z<0.4) & =Φ(0.4)-Φ(-0.1) \\  & =0.6554-0.4602 \\  & =0.1952 \\  & ≈0.20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected flight lasts more than $178$ minutes but less than $188$ minutes is approximately $0.20.$

Question 9
?

The durations of direct flights on a certain route are normally distributed with a mean of 180 minutes and a standard deviation of 20 minutes. What is the probability that a randomly selected flight lasts more than 178 minutes but less than 188 minutes? Round your answer to two decimal places.

Hint: A table of values of Φ(z) for different values of z is given below, where Φ(z) is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.

EXPLANATION

Let X represent the flight duration (in minutes). Then we have X∼N(180,202).

We want to find P(178<X<188). First, we convert X to a standard normal random variable by z-scoring:

P(178<X<188)=P(178−18020<Z<188−18020)=P(−0.1<Z<0.4)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of Φ(z):

P(−0.1<Z<0.4)=P(Z<0.4)−P(Z≤−0.1)=P(Z≤0.4)−P(Z≤−0.1)=Φ(0.4)−Φ(−0.1)

From the z-table, we see that

Φ(0.4)=0.6554Φ(−0.1)=0.4602.

So, we have

P(−0.1<Z<0.4)=Φ(0.4)−Φ(−0.1)=0.6554−0.4602=0.1952≈0.20

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected flight lasts more than 178 minutes but less than 188 minutes is approximately 0.20.
